newsitem.title: UK: UK electricity grid to handle near-record demand.
newsitem.headline: UK electricity grid to handle near-record demand.

text.p: British electricity demand on Monday will approach but not exceed last year's record as temperatures rise, the National Grid said.

The Grid spokeswoman said that electricity demand was expected to peak at "in excess of 48,000 MegaWatts (mW)" at between 17.00 and 17.30 GMT. But she added that it was not expected to reach the record set last January of 48,811 mW.
She agreed that there had been discussion last week of possible record demand if the cold weather continued into this week.
Higher demand had been expected on Monday -- the first day of full strength demand from businesses and industry after the extended Christmas and New Year break.

The spokeswoman said that the system has the notional capacity to deliver 60,000 mW of electric power at any given moment, although "we can't always call on all of that" because of the possibility of outages or maintenance.
But she could not say what capacity is available at present. The 60,000 mW total includes 2,000 mW delivered by subsea cable from France, and this is already coming in to Britain's National Grid.
